text.p: These are some of the main stories in Sofia newspapers today. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

-- Protesters blocked with cars and human chains the main road from Sofia to Kulata checkpoint at the border with Greece in support of strikes called by trade unions against formation of a new Socialist government and for early parliamentary elections. @

-- The ruling Socialist Party's executive bureau proposed to the outgoing cabinet to raise salaries of public employees, pensions and social payments by 100 percent, socialist deputy Petar Dimitrov said.
-- Trains in Bulgaria stopped for one hour on Wednesday for the first time since the 1919 general railway workers' strike in support of nationwide strikes called by trade unions.

-- Bulgaria risks losing preferential conditions on the Iraqi market if it agrees to sell a $2 billion debt owed by Baghdad to a third party, Vassil Vassilev, chairman of the Bulgarian-Iraqi consortium said. @

-- Citizens have withrawn some 10 billion levs from the State Savings Bank (SSB) since the beginning of the week due to the slump of the lev against the dollar, SSB executive director Bistra Dimitrova said.

-- Bulgaria might have to default on its foreign debt payments later this year unless it receives urgent finacial support for its collapsing economy from the West, Bulgaria's president Petar Stoyanov said in Brussels.

-- Bulgaria's private construction enterpreneur Solomon Angel was arrested on charges of misappropriation of some 200 million levs from more than 300 clients who paid in advance for apartments in Sofia that still have not been built.
-- Bulgarian students organised a torchlight protest rally in central Sofia to press for early elections and held a spoof Miss Protest and Mister Vagabond contests.
-- Bulgaria's outgoing cabinet is expected to discuss today a possible rise of fuel prices, a government's Price Committee official said but declined to give details.
